questions.question: <div style=\"text-align:justify\">Which of the following statements about the chemical behavior of amines is **INCORRECT <\/strong>?<\/div>$\n$
options: Primary aliphatic amines, when heated with chloroform and alcoholic KOH, produce foul-smelling isocyanides, while secondary and tertiary amines do not undergo this reaction.
Secondary amines react with nitrous acid to form yellow, oily N-nitrosoamines, whereas primary aromatic amines form stable diazonium salts at 0–5°C (273–278 K).
Primary amines react with benzenesulphonyl chloride to form sulphonamides that are soluble in alkali due to the presence of an acidic hydrogen on the nitrogen.
Tertiary amines react with benzenesulphonyl chloride to form water-soluble sulphonamide salts under neutral conditions.
questions.explanation:
A: Primary aliphatic amines form isocyanides (R–NC) via carbylamine test; secondary/tertiary amines don’t react.
$ B$: Secondary amines form N-nitrosoamines (R2N–NO); primary aromatic amines form diazonium salts at 0–5°C.
$ C$: Primary amines form sulphonamides (R–NH–SO2C6H5), soluble in alkali due to acidic N–H.
$ D$: Tertiary amines (R3N) do not form sulphonamides with benzenesulphonyl chloride, as they lack N–H; no “sulphonamide salts” are formed.
$ $
$ $

questions.question: <div style=\"text-align:justify\">**Statement I : <\/strong>The metabolism of chloroform in the liver produces phosgene, a highly toxic gas, which contributes to its toxicity, whereas dichloromethane’s neurotoxic effects, such as impaired hearing and vision, are primarily due to its interaction with the central nervous system.<br \/>$\n$**Statement II : <\/strong>The storage of chloroform in dark-colored, air-free bottles is critical to prevent its oxidative transformation into phosgene, which is not a concern for dichloromethane due to its lower susceptibility to atmospheric oxidation.<\/div>$\n$
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
questions.explanation: <div style=\"text-align:justify\">Chloroform is metabolized to phosgene in the liver, causing hepatotoxicity, while dichloromethane directly affects the central nervous system, impairing hearing and vision, without such metabolic transformation. Chloroform requires storage in closed, dark-colored, air-free bottles to prevent oxidation to phosgene, unlike dichloromethane, which lacks similar storage precautions.<\/div>$\n$

questions.question: <div style=\"text-align:justify\">In the reaction 5A + 3B→4C, 1.0 mole of A (molar mass 10 g\/mol) and 0.9 moles of B (molar mass 20 g\/mol) are dissolved in a solvent to form a 0.5-liter solution. The reaction goes to completion, volume remains constant, then diluted to 2 liters. Another side reaction consumes 20% of C (molar mass 30 g\/mol) to form an inert byproduct. What is the mass of C in the final solution?<\/div>$\n$
questions.explanation:
**Limiting Reagent
$ Reaction$: 5A + 3B→4C
$ Given$: A = 1.0 mol, B = 0.9 mol
$ Required$ A for 0.9 mol B = (5/3) × 0.9 = 1.5 mol
$ A$ is limiting
$ $**Moles of C Produced: 1.0 mol A → (4/5) × 1.0 = **0.8 mol C
$ Side$ Reaction Loss: 80% of C remains: 0.8 × 0.8 = **0.64 mol C,
$ Mass$ of C 0.64 mol × 30 g/mol = **19.2 g
$ $
